Scenarios.Scenario: An extension calls the new Repository.rebaseContinue API after resolving and staging a conflicted rebase.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ApiRepository.rebaseContinue delegates to Repository.rebaseContinue, which waits for one `git rebase --continue` subprocess and then the standard non-read-only repository model refresh before the promise resolves. This work is on the API call's critical path by design.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one subprocess per API invocation; there is no loop or collection fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The low-level operation and internal commit-driven continue path already existed, but extensions had no direct public rebaseContinue entry point.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the rebaseContinue promise can resolve.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refreshes HEAD/branch information, status, and refs after the mutation; first use may also read the virtual-filesystem config.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One standard refresh per invocation, with a bounded set of repository-wide Git commands; status and refs run in parallel after the initial state probes. Cardinality does not scale with conflict-file count at this layer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All existing non-read-only Repository.run operations, including the internal rebase-continue path, already performed the same refresh; only the public caller route is new.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The API promise waits for the standard post-mutation refresh so exposed repository state is current.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reads repository config/worktree metadata and probes REBASE_HEAD, rebase-apply, rebase-merge, MERGE_HEAD, and CHERRY_PICK_HEAD during model refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A bounded repository-wide set per refresh; the three rebase probes execute concurrently and do not scale with changed-file count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The refresh and probe count already existed; the diff only corrects the git-directory base path for linked worktrees and submodules.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs in parallel with other initial state probes before status and refs are collected.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of explicit API invocations. Each invocation represents one logical rebase continuation and performs one continuation subprocess plus one existing repository-wide refresh; conflict-file count does not multiply boundary calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Within a refresh, independent state probes are intentionally parallel, followed by parallel status and refs reads. Repository operations are tracked but this method adds no loop, Promise.all fan-out, or new aggregate scheduler burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Mutable Git state is refreshed rather than cached. The virtual-filesystem config probe is cached after first initialization; no new cache keys, negative-cache behavior, or cache retention is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the delegate, operation wrapper, subprocess call, and post-operation refresh are directly traced in the repository code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Git command duration depends on hooks, repository size, and the remaining rebase sequence, but those costs are inherent to the explicitly requested operation and existing refresh path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new boundary is the single operation explicitly requested by the API caller, and the remaining work is the established bounded refresh with no changed fan-out or scheduling mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Automatic or manual status refresh in a normal repository after file changes or Git operations.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Repository.status enters the existing throttled Repository.run path and refreshes model state. The changed marker probes remain part of the parallel initial-state phase before status and refs complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Per refresh, performs two existence checks and one REBASE_HEAD read plus MERGE_HEAD and CHERRY_PICK_HEAD existence checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Five bounded marker probes per repository refresh, independent of file count; the rebase trio runs concurrently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: For an ordinary non-bare repository, `<root>/.git` and `dotGit.path` identify the same directory, so both call count and target are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The probes are in the model-refresh critical path but overlap the HEAD, remotes, submodules, worktrees, template, and VFS probes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Runs the existing repository-wide Git status/refs and HEAD-related reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A bounded set per throttled refresh; status processes the repository once rather than once per file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Determines when updated SCM state is published.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of opened repositories and debounced/throttled refreshes, not number of files for the changed marker-path logic.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: File-change refresh requests are debounced by 1 second and throttled with an additional 5-second wait; initial status across repositories uses the existing initial-status limiter. State probes within one repository are parallel.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Marker state is intentionally read fresh because rebase/merge/cherry-pick state is mutable. No cache behavior changes for ordinary repositories.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both old and new path expressions resolve to the repository's `.git` directory in this scenario.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filesystem latency can vary, especially on remote filesystems, but the diff changes neither operation count nor paths for ordinary repositories.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance change for normal repositories.

Scenarios.Scenario: Status refresh for a linked worktree or submodule, including while a rebase is stopped on conflicts.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The standard refresh now probes the worktree/submodule-specific git directory. When REBASE_HEAD and a rebase state directory exist, getRebaseCommit additionally waits for one `git show -s` of the stopped commit so SCM state can expose rebaseCommit.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Probes rebase state in `repository.dotGit.path`, the per-worktree or submodule Git directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two existence checks and one small file read per refresh, in parallel; count is constant per repository.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same three probes existed but targeted `<root>/.git/...`, which is not the repository-specific Git directory for linked worktrees and can be a file. The diff changes their target, not their count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Correctly detects active rebase state during the initial parallel refresh phase.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Runs one `git show -s` to obtain metadata for REBASE_HEAD when a linked-worktree or submodule rebase is active.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one per refresh and only while valid rebase state is present; no per-conflict or per-commit fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The invalid old path caused linked-worktree/submodule rebase detection to return undefined, so this commit lookup was not reached in that case. Main repositories already performed it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds bounded latency to active-rebase refreshes in exchange for publishing the previously unavailable rebase commit state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Checks merge and cherry-pick marker files in the correct per-worktree/submodule Git directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two existence checks per refresh, constant per repository.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same checks existed at invalid `<root>/.git/...` paths for these repository kinds; only the target path changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs in parallel with the other initial state probes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of linked repositories being refreshed and refresh frequency. During an active rebase, each affected repository adds at most one commit-metadata subprocess per refresh, independent of conflict count and rebase history length.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-repository marker checks overlap through Promise.all; automatic refresh is debounced/throttled, and startup status uses the existing cross-repository limiter. No new per-item concurrency is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is used for active operation markers because they must reflect external Git changes. Cold and warm refreshes have the same bounded probes; commit metadata is read only after positive rebase-state detection.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the corrected dotGit path, positive-state branch, and single getCommit subprocess are explicit in the changed and surrounding code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A `git show -s` can vary with object storage and remote filesystem latency, but it is one bounded local Git read only during an active rebase. No evidence indicates a material latency regression relative to the required linked-worktree state reporting.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance issue. The only newly reachable subprocess is bounded to one per active-rebase refresh and is necessary to provide the corrected rebase state; there is no multiplicative or unbounded mechanism.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files and traced the new API, operation scheduler, Git subprocess, model refresh, status triggers, and worktree/submodule marker paths. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced, and the pull request does not establish a shipped performance-regression fix requiring blame.
